text:
Ellie: Heads-up — OpenFlux just pushed V2 weights and their legal sent a weird hosting clause. They want us to be able to serve inference but not redistribute the weights to third parties. Link: https://openflux.ai/partners/v2
Sanjay: can you paste the clause?
Ellie: quick paste: `NonRedistribute-HostOnly v1.0` — allowed: host for inference, generate outputs; prohibited: provide model weights, rehost for resale, or package in customer-onprem bundles.
Kate: ok from partnerships POV that’s doable, but marketplace listing and HW bundles are trickier. We need explicit marketplace rights and a packaging exception for certified SI partners.
Liam: ML note — V2 is quant-friendly but we do some conversion/quant steps on our side. Does the clause cover derived artifacts? i.e., a 4-bit quantized version we generate for serving?
Arya: legal opinion (short): clause as written forbids redistribution of the underlying weights or derived artifacts unless a written redistribution license is provided. Hosting/serving is allowed if we do not expose the checkpoint. We can negotiate a narrow "SI bundle" exception.
Jen: sales concern — some of our customers (on-prem SI deployments) will want a packaged appliance. If we can get an SI bundle exception limited to named integrators and timeboxed, that might be fine.
Ellie: proposal: request these three carve-outs from OpenFlux: 1) named-SI redistribution exception (timeboxed), 2) marketplace SKU hosting permission (we can list & bill), 3) permission to create internal quantized serving variants for inference only.
PartnerOpsBot: /remind #partnerships to circle back with OpenFlux legal in 48h :bell:
Sanjay: will draft an email to their counsel. Also need to confirm export control (EAR/ITAR) provenance because some modules have encryption keys.
Arya: yes include export control questionnaire. Ask for model provenance statement and training data high-level description (no raw datasets).
Liam: ops detail — if SI bundle is agreed, we should require SI to use our private container image and our runtime so we never ship weights. That protects their compliance posture.
Kate: agree. Also add a SKU mapping table for marketplace: e.g., `openflux-v2-hosted`, `openflux-v2-dedicated` and `openflux-v2-private` and whether each SKU permits fine-tuning/embeddings. Need OpenFlux to confirm allowed features per SKU.
Ellie: drafting email now — aiming to: (a) ask for redistribution carve-outs, (b) ask for provenance & export questionnaire, (c) ask whether attribution/announcements are co-marketable and joint-press windows.
Jen: announcement note — marketing wants 2-week embargo from agreement signing, prefer a joint quote. Please get point of contact at OpenFlux PM for quotes.
Sanjay: rough draft of the ask (will paste):
```
Hi OpenFlux legal + product — thank you for V2. We can host the model under NonRedistribute-HostOnly v1.0 but need clarifications/limited carve-outs to support the Redwood marketplace and SI go-to-market. Specifically:
1) Named-SI redistribution exception (time-limited, non-transferable)
2) Explicit marketplace listing permission for hosted and dedicated SKUs
3) Permission to create internal quantized variants for serving (not distributable)
4) Model provenance and export-control questionnaire
5) Co-announcement approval and PR window details
Please advise who on your side can sign off or discuss next week. — Redwood Partnerships
```
Arya: fine, add a clause asking for indemnity language around customer misuse? Or at least warranty disclaimers. Keep it light, ask for their standard wording.
Ellie: will send in 30m. Quick sync? 15m after I send to triage replies.
Kate: I'll block 30m on calendar with Jen + Arya + Liam.
Sanjay: ping me on thread once sent, I'll loop infra and marketplace owners.
Jen: I'll prep a marketing checklist: press quote, embargo date options, partner logos, joint webinar window.
Ellie: sent — thread now includes OpenFlux legal (CCed) and PM. Moving conversation to vendor channel once they reply. Thanks all. :party_parrot:
